subject: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist — next steps and SDK/auth questions
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — VPC connectivity & integration next steps

Hi Alex / Sana — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track items for your network team and our SREs.

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- Private connectivity: VPC endpoints (AWS) or private peering to avoid public egress for inference calls
- IP allowlist: control-plane and data-plane IP ranges for firewall rules
- Egress/DNS: ensure egress to Redwood endpoints is allowed, and need to support DNS resolution for internal hostnames if using VPC endpoints
- mTLS: your security team asked about mutual TLS as an auth option for dedicated/private deployments
- SDK/auth: plan to use our SDK + short-lived tokens (or mTLS certs if you prefer) for service-to-service calls
- Routing & fallbacks: prefer regional routing with fallback to a secondary region in case of outages
- Structured output/tool-calling/embeddings: want to confirm support for structured JSON outputs + embeddings/reranker pipeline for semantic search use cases

Attachments:
- redwood-vpc-integration-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
- networking-diagram.png (image/png)

Proposed next steps / asks for your team:
1) Please share the network team's IP allowlist window: are you able to accept a range of IPs (we can provide single-region and multi-region ranges) or do you need a fixed set of addresses?
2) Do you want to evaluate token-based auth first, or pursue mTLS for mutual auth? If mTLS, we'll loop Jonas (solutions eng) to help with cert exchange and CA expectations.
3) Any constraints on egress/DNS (e.g., blocked external DNS, requirement to use internal DNS resolvers)? If so, tell us the resolver IPs and we can validate with our infra team.
4) For embeddings/reranker: please confirm expected index size and QPS so we can recommend Dedicated vs Hosted with VPC access.

I've looped in our solutions engineer Jonas Weber (jonas.weber@redwood.ai) to answer technical network questions. Marissa will continue as the AE for procurement/contract questions.

Would you be available early next week (Mon/Tue) for a 30-min follow-up with your network/SRE? I can propose times once you confirm availability.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren — this is great, very clear. A few quick answers from our side: 

1) IP allowlist: our security team prefers a fixed set of CIDR ranges they can allow in our firewall rules. Can you provide both single-region and multi-region range sets?
2) Auth: we'd like to pursue mTLS for the data-plane if possible (we have an internal PKI). For control-plane/console access we'll use SSO.
3) DNS/egress: our environment uses an internal DNS resolver (10.10.0.10) and outbound proxy that only allows traffic to approved hosts.
4) Embeddings/reranker: initial index ~2M documents, QPS for semantic search expected ~20 req/s at peak. We want latency under 200ms for top-K retrieval + reranker.

We'll attach a spreadsheet with our network constraints — sharing this with our SREs and will schedule a follow-up with them.

Alex

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick answers and the constraints doc. Some clarifications and what we'll prepare before the follow-up call with your SREs: 

Network & connectivity
- We'll provide two IP set options: (A) single-region CIDRs and (B) consolidated multi-region CIDRs. For mTLS-enabled private deployments we can also publish a smaller, stable set of egress addresses for your firewall.
- DNS: we support two modes — (1) VPC endpoints with private DNS (preferred) where we can resolve hostnames inside your VPC, and (2) egress-to-public endpoints if you prefer to proxy/allow specific hostnames. Given you have an internal resolver at 10.10.0.10, Jonas will validate whether private DNS can chain to your resolver or if we should rely on endpoint-level A records.
- Egress/proxy: we can work with your outbound proxy. We will provide the exact FQDNs and IPs our nodes will use and we can also support TLS SNI allowlisting so you don't have to rely on IPs alone.

Auth & certs
- mTLS: we can authenticate using client certs. If you have an internal PKI, we can accept client certs signed by your CA and configure our endpoints to require them. Jonas will follow up with the required cert formats, CSR flow, and TTL expectations.
- Tokens: alternatively, our SDK supports short-lived JWT bearer tokens minted by your IdP (via OIDC). This is faster to pilot but less strictly mutual-authenticated.

SDK/routing/structured output
- SDK setup: we have a Node + Python SDK. Example quickstart will be provided in the shared Drive link. It supports automatic region-aware routing and can be pinned to a specific endpoint for private deployments.
- Structured output / tool calling: Redwood supports structured JSON outputs and tool-calling patterns (we can provide a sample schema and a conversation-to-tool mapping).
- Embeddings & reranker: given ~2M documents and 20 QPS peak, we'd recommend Dedicated capacity with autoscale configured for your burst profile. We'll propose a batching config that keeps latency near your 200ms target. Reranker can run on the same dedicated pool or a smaller dedicated config depending on cost/latency tradeoffs.

Deliverables we'll send before the SRE call:
- IP allowlist options (single-region & multi-region) + FQDNs and SNI names
- mTLS cert integration checklist (cert formats, CSR example, rotation cadence)
- Example SDK quickstart with region pinning and token + mTLS examples
- Initial Dedicated sizing recommendation for embeddings/reranker based on 2M docs and 20 QPS

Would Monday 3/9 at 11:00am PT work for a 30-min technical sync with Jonas and our infra team? If not, propose two alternatives and we'll lock in a time.

Thanks — looping Jonas to start drafting the cert checklist.

Best,
Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
